summary: Frontend-only retest for AdminShell sidebar redesign (220px width, no truncation, thin gold themed scrollbar) and PublicShell fan logout regression. All criteria met: sidebar exactly 220px, all 20 nav items present with full labels (CALENDARIO/CLASSIFICHE etc.), no ellipsis/overflow, nav has fsl-scroll class with scrollbarWidth='thin'. Mobile drawer at 390px shows complete labels, scrollable (958 > 671), thin themed scrollbar (visually confirmed via screenshot - no gray system bar with arrows). Fan logout from /account now lands on / (public hub) with anonymous header (public-area-societa-link + public-fan-register-link visible, no fan-notifications-button) and stays anonymous after reload. Regression: anon /account → /login OK; fan re-login → /account with public-fan-account-link and fan-notifications-button visible.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminShell renders the same <aside data-testid='admin-sidebar'> twice at <xl breakpoints (one inside 'hidden xl:block' desktop container, another inside the mobile drawer). Both carry the same data-testid, causing duplicate nodes for every sidebar-nav-* testid. Automated tests picking the first match hit the display:none copy. Consider giving the mobile drawer copy a distinct data-testid (e.g. admin-sidebar-drawer) or rendering only one instance conditionally to keep testids unique.
